title: Movie theaters must provide audio, visual aids for people with disabilities: Supreme Court
bullets: South Korea's Supreme Court ruled that movie theaters must provide audio and visual assistance for people with visual or hearing impairments.
The court overturned an appellate ruling that had limited the required assistance to auditoriums with at least 300 seats and only 3 percent of screenings.
Four plaintiffs with disabilities originally filed the lawsuit in 2016 against major theater chains CGV, Lotte Cultureworks, and Megabox JoongAng.

title: Seoul shares extend gains late Thu. morning as oil prices ease
bullets: South Korea's benchmark stock index rose 1.4 percent late Thursday morning, recovering from a steep drop in the previous session.
Shares gained as oil prices eased after U.S. President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived.
Major South Korean companies, including Samsung Electronics, Hyundai Motor, and LG Energy Solution, saw their stock prices increase.

title: 6 missing, 1 dead after tugboat capsizes off Busan
bullets: A tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized and sank off the coast of Busan.
One crew member died, one was rescued, and six others remain missing.
Authorities deployed vessels and aircraft to search for the missing crew, but strong waves and currents are hampering the operation.

title: Intensive search under way for 9 S. Koreans missing in Nepal floods
bullets: A 44-member South Korean disaster relief team arrived in Nepal to help search for victims missing after massive floods and landslides.
Nine South Koreans went missing on August 26 while working at a hydropower plant construction site in Nepal's Rasuwa district.
South Korea is providing rescue dogs, advanced search equipment, DNA testing tools, and approximately 38,000 blankets to support the relief efforts.

A feature titled "Wonder Hours with Hyerim" listed ten reasons to date AxMxP on August 26, 2026.
A K-POP News segment published on August 31, 2026, highlighted music comebacks scheduled for September.

title: Hyundai cooling film takes heat off police buses
bullets: Hyundai Motor Group installed its transparent Nano Cooling Film on two Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency buses.
The film reflects solar heat and releases interior heat, keeping the bus interior about 2 to 3 degrees Celsius cooler on average.
Hyundai plans to monitor the buses for one year before deciding whether to start full-scale production.

title: Gyeonggi support center aids over 700 migrant women in 1st year after opening
bullets: Between August 2025 and June 2026, the Gyeonggi Foreign Women’s Counseling Center provided 6,101 counseling sessions to 712 migrant women.
The center assists foreign women facing domestic abuse, legal anxieties, and financial stress, operating regardless of their immigration status.
Provincial leaders plan to expand counseling hubs into northern Gyeonggi and recruit interpreters for rare dialects to improve accessibility.

title: Lee orders to mobilize all available resources to search, rescue crew of capsized tugboat
bullets: A 286-ton tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized off the coast of Busan on Wednesday afternoon.
Rescuers saved two crew members, leaving one unconscious, while six others remain missing.
President Lee Jae Myung and Prime Minister Han Seong-sook ordered all available resources to be mobilized for the rescue efforts.

title: Voice phishing crimes drop 40 pct thanks to tougher measures
bullets: The government implemented special measures to fight voice phishing, such as emergency phone number blocking, AI warning systems, and international cooperation.
Voice phishing cases continuously declined for 10 consecutive months from October to July, falling 39.9 percent on-year to 12,554 cases.
Financial losses from voice phishing crimes dropped 43.2 percent to 632.4 billion won during the same period.

title: Veterans ministry seeks 8 pct hike in 2027 budget for expanded honors, key projects
bullets: South Korea's Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs has proposed a 7.22 trillion won budget for next year, representing an 8 percent increase.
The plan expands financial benefits for war veterans and independence fighters' descendants while lowering the age threshold for using veterans hospitals from 75 to 65.
The proposed budget will also fund turning Hyochang Park into a national cemetery and preparing for the 2029 Invictus Games in Daejeon.

title: Cortis’ ‘Redred’ best K-pop song this summer: TikTok
bullets: Cortis' song "Redred" topped TikTok's Songs of the Summer 2026 list for Korea, and the group was named Boyband of the Summer.
The track is the lead single from their second EP "Greengreen," which entered the Billboard 200 chart at No. 3.
Cortis is scheduled to perform three concerts in Yokohama, Japan, starting Friday for their "Put Your Phone Down" tour.

title: 2 rescued, 6 missing after tugboat capsizes in waters off Busan
bullets: A 286-ton tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized in the waters off Busan on Wednesday afternoon.
Two crew members have been rescued so far, while six others remain missing.
President Lee Jae Myung instructed authorities to mobilize all available resources for search and rescue operations.

title: Korea moves to protect migrant fishermen from forced labor
bullets: South Korea's government issued updated guidelines to help law enforcement identify and protect migrant fishermen from forced labor and human trafficking.
The new framework sets clear warning signs of physical, emotional, and financial coercion tailored specifically to the maritime fishing industry.
Officials aim to use these rules to spot labor abuses at ports before ships leave for isolated waters.

title: Korea overhauls child protection system after death of 11-year-old
bullets: South Korea announced a major overhaul of its child protection system after an 11-year-old disabled child died from fatal abuse.
The new guidelines require police and local child protection officers to share real-time report details and perform mandatory joint site visits.
The government will automatically prioritize removing a child from any household that receives two or more abuse reports within a year.

title: Korea seeks to toughen pension eligibility for foreign residents as loophole found
bullets: South Korea is tightening its national pension rules for foreign residents after a loophole allowed them to secure benefits through lump-sum retroactive payments.
A government investigation identified three foreign applicants who used this back-payment scheme, but only one is currently receiving a pension.
Under new regulations, retroactive payments are only allowed for months in which a foreign resident stayed in South Korea for at least 15 days.

title: Court approves corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus
bullets: A Seoul court approved a corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus Co. after creditors and shareholders voted in favor of it.
The discount store chain previously filed for rehabilitation due to liquidity concerns and a declining credit rating.
Under the approved plan, Homeplus aims to sell 19 closed stores by February 2028 to repay debts totaling 1.3 trillion won.

title: Busan film festival unveils 315-film lineup for 31st edition
bullets: The 31st Busan International Film Festival will screen 315 films from 59 countries, making it the festival's largest lineup since 2019.
The festival is now an Oscar-qualifying event, allowing the winner of its best film award to qualify for the Oscar for best international feature.
This year's edition places a major focus on animation and will host international guests including Michelle Yeoh and Maggie Gyllenhaal.

title: South Korea’s Oceans Ministry unveils record 2027 budget to drive maritime growth
bullets: South Korea’s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has proposed a record 82.6 trillion won budget for 2027. This represents a 10.8 percent increase from the previous year.
The proposed funds will be used for port infrastructure development, smart aquaculture, artificial intelligence cargo systems, and marine technology research.
Environmental programs in the plan focus on fighting illegal fishing, using robotic systems to collect marine waste, and expanding coastal carbon storage projects.

title: S. Korea dispatches disaster relief team to Nepal to support flood recovery efforts
bullets: South Korea dispatched a 44-person disaster relief team to Nepal to support search and rescue efforts following severe floods. The team will stay in Nepal for about 10 days to help locate victims using specialized equipment and search dogs.

The massive floods and mudslides in Nepal killed over 800 people and left nine South Korean power plant workers missing in Rasuwa district. A South Korean rapid response team is already on the ground conducting joint searches with the Nepali military.

Rescue workers recently recovered one unidentified body from a tunnel at the hydropower plant site where the missing South Koreans were working. Officials are currently working through diplomatic channels to confirm the identity and nationality of the victim.
